thought:
To create a 'Base Reference' establishing shot for the 'Summit Position' on Langya Mountain, the prompt must focus on the tactical nature of the geography without including any characters. The key visual elements are the specific improvised weapons (rolling logs and stones) and the topography (steep drop, defensive high ground). 

I will use a high-angle wide shot to establish the height and the danger of the terrain. The composition will place the defensive stockpiles in the foreground to emphasize the 'trap' aspect, while the background will show the steep path to illustrate the enemy's approach vector. The lighting should be harsh and natural to reflect the high altitude and the gritty reality of 1941 warfare. The style will be photorealistic and cinematic, mimicking a historical war film with high textural detail on the rocks and wood.
prompt: Cinematic wide-angle establishing shot of a rugged, desolate mountain summit defensive position. High-angle perspective looking downward towards a perilous cliff edge. Composition features large defensive stockpiles of heavy round timber logs and heaps of jagged rocks arranged in the foreground and midground as 'rolling stone' weapons. Natural jagged limestone rock formations form a crude rampart. Beyond the cliff edge, a dizzyingly steep, winding, treacherous mountain path is visible extending downwards into the abyss. Harsh high-altitude daylight, sharp cast shadows, gritty dust particles in the air, tense atmosphere. Realistic historical film still, 1941 war drama style, authentic texture, matte earth tones, deep depth of field, highly detailed rock textures. ratio 1:1
